questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, quite significantly, and I think this is something most people experience intuitively even if they don't consciously reflect on it. For me personally, I find that being in spaces with warm, earthy tones—deep greens, terracotta, warm browns—creates a sense of calm and groundedness that I find conducive to focused work. Bright, saturated colours like yellow or orange tend to feel energising and uplifting, which is why I gravitate toward them when I want to feel more alert. Conversely, cold, clinical environments dominated by harsh whites or greys can feel draining and impersonal. I've become quite deliberate about the colours in my immediate environment as a result—choosing warm lighting and natural tones for my study space, for example.

questions.sampleBand9: That's an interesting question. While there are certainly conventional associations between colours and genders, I think it's becoming increasingly blurred. Traditionally speaking, men were more likely to favour darker, more subdued colours, perhaps reflecting a sense of practicality or even stoicism. Women, on the other hand, were often drawn to brighter, more vibrant hues. questions.sampleAnswer: Research does suggest some consistent patterns in colour preferences between men and women, though I think it's important to acknowledge that these are statistical tendencies rather than universal rules, and that cultural conditioning plays a significant role. Studies have found that women tend to report a broader range of favourite colours and show a stronger preference for softer, more nuanced shades—pastels, muted tones, and colours with names that distinguish subtle variations. Men, on average, tend to prefer bolder, more saturated colours and show a stronger preference for blue in particular. However, many researchers argue that these differences are largely the product of socialisation rather than innate biological differences—the association of pink with girls and blue with boys, for example, is a relatively recent cultural convention that varies across societies. I think individual personality, cultural background, and personal experience are far more powerful determinants of colour preference than gender.

questions.sampleAnswer:
I'd like to describe a presentation I gave approximately two years ago to a group of about forty university students and faculty members at an academic seminar.

The audience was a mixed group—mostly students from my department, along with several professors and a few visiting researchers. It was a relatively formal academic setting, which added a degree of pressure that a more casual presentation wouldn't have had.

The presentation was about the impact of social media on political polarisation—specifically, how algorithmic content curation on platforms like Facebook and Twitter tends to create what researchers call 'filter bubbles', where users are predominantly exposed to information and opinions that confirm their existing beliefs. I had been researching this topic for several months as part of a larger project, and the seminar was an opportunity to present my preliminary findings and receive feedback from peers and supervisors.

The reason I gave the presentation was partly academic—it was a required component of my research programme—but also because I genuinely believed the topic was important and wanted to contribute to the conversation happening in my department about the social effects of digital technology. I had put considerable effort into preparing the presentation: researching the existing literature, organising my arguments clearly, and creating visual aids that would help the audience follow the more complex statistical elements.

In terms of how I felt, the experience was a mixture of anxiety and excitement. In the days leading up to it, I was genuinely nervous—public speaking in an academic context, where your audience includes people who know the subject deeply, is particularly daunting. I worried about being asked questions I couldn't answer, or about failing to communicate complex ideas clearly enough. However, once I began speaking, I found that my preparation gave me a solid foundation and my anxiety diminished fairly quickly. I became absorbed in the content and in the interaction with the audience.

The reception was encouraging—several people asked thoughtful questions that pushed my thinking further, and one of the professors suggested a methodological approach I hadn't considered, which was genuinely useful. Afterwards, I felt a strong sense of accomplishment and relief. The experience reinforced something important for me: that the anxiety before a public presentation is almost always worse than the experience itself, and that thorough preparation is the most effective antidote to that anxiety. It also gave me more confidence in my ability to communicate complex ideas to a knowledgeable audience, which is a skill I continue to work on.

Tomoshabinlar aralash guruh edi - asosan mening kafedramdan talabalar, bir nechta professorlar va bir nechta tashrif buyurgan tadqiqotchilar. Bu nisbatan rasmiy akademik muhit edi, bu esa oddiyroq taqdimotda bo'lmagan bosimni oshirdi.

O'zimni qanday his qilganim nuqtai nazaridan, tajriba xavotir va hayajon aralashmasi edi. Unga tayyorgarlik ko'rish kunlarida men chinakam asabiylashdim - auditoriyangiz ushbu mavzuni chuqur biladigan odamlarni o'z ichiga olgan akademik kontekstda ommaviy nutq so'zlash ayniqsa qo'rqinchli. Biroq, gapira boshlaganimdan so'ng, tayyorgarligim menga mustahkam asos berganini va xavotirim tezda kamayganini angladim. Men mazmunga va tomoshabinlar bilan o'zaro aloqaga sho'ng'ib ketdim.

questions.sampleBand9: Without a doubt, I consider public speaking an indispensable skill in today's world. questions.sampleAnswer: Absolutely, and I'd argue it's one of the most valuable skills a person can develop, regardless of their profession. Beyond the professional sphere, public speaking builds confidence in communication generally, which benefits personal relationships and civic participation. I also think the process of preparing a speech—organising your thoughts, anticipating questions, distilling complex ideas into clear language—is itself a valuable cognitive exercise that sharpens thinking and communication across all contexts.

questions.prompt: How has technology changed the way people give presentations?

questions.sampleBand7: Technology has completely transformed presentations. Obviously, we've moved away from things like flip charts and slide projectors. questions.sampleBand8: Well, I think technology has revolutionised how we give presentations, fundamentally. It's a world away from the days of handwritten notes and clunky projectors. This opens up possibilities for more engaging and impactful presentations, but it also means presenters need to be more tech-savvy.
questions.sampleBand9: Technology has profoundly reshaped the presentation landscape, moving it far beyond static slides and death by PowerPoint. Moreover, real-time data integration and audience polling capabilities allow for dynamic adaptation and personalized delivery. The only caveat is that the technology should enhance, not overshadow, the core message and the presenter's connection with the audience; falling back on gimmicks can be counterproductive.
questions.sampleAnswer: Technology has transformed presentations in several significant ways. The most obvious is the shift from physical materials—handwritten notes, overhead projectors, printed slides—to digital tools like PowerPoint, Keynote, and more recently, sophisticated platforms that allow for interactive, multimedia-rich presentations. This has raised the visual standard of presentations considerably, though it's also created new problems—the phenomenon of 'death by PowerPoint', where presenters hide behind excessive slides rather than engaging directly with their audience, is a genuine issue. Video conferencing technology has also changed presentations fundamentally—the ability to present to audiences anywhere in the world without travelling has made presentations more accessible but also more challenging in terms of maintaining engagement. More recently, AI tools are beginning to assist with presentation preparation—generating content, suggesting structures, and even providing real-time feedback on delivery. The core challenge, however, remains the same: communicating ideas clearly and compellingly to an audience.

questions.prompt: What benefits does the Internet bring to communication?

Businesses, in particular, have benefited from streamlined communication channels, enabling them to stay ahead of the curve in a competitive global market. It's a double-edged sword, naturally, but the advantages are undeniable, and in the grand scheme of things, the internet has been a boon for communication.
questions.sampleAnswer: The Internet has transformed communication in ways that are genuinely revolutionary, and the benefits are substantial. The most fundamental is the elimination of distance as a barrier—people can now communicate instantly with anyone anywhere in the world at essentially no cost, which was unimaginable a generation ago. This has profound implications for personal relationships, enabling families and friends separated by geography to maintain close connections through video calls, messaging, and social media. For professional communication, the Internet has enabled new forms of collaboration—teams can work together across time zones, share documents in real time, and coordinate complex projects without being in the same physical location. The democratisation of communication is another significant benefit—anyone with internet access can now publish ideas, reach a global audience, and participate in public discourse in ways that were previously restricted to those with access to traditional media. The Internet has also accelerated the spread of information, enabling rapid responses to crises, the sharing of scientific knowledge, and the coordination of social movements.

questions.sampleBand9: Well, undoubtedly, several qualities are essential. Articulation and clarity are paramount; the ability to convey complex ideas in a simple, accessible manner is crucial. Furthermore, empathy and emotional intelligence play a significant role. Being able to pick up on non-verbal cues and adapt your communication style accordingly is key. At the end of the day, communication is about connection, and these qualities foster that connection.
questions.sampleAnswer: Effective communication requires a constellation of qualities that work together. Clarity of thought is perhaps the most fundamental—you can only communicate clearly what you understand clearly yourself, which means good communicators invest time in organising and refining their thinking before expressing it. Active listening is equally important and often underrated—the best communicators are genuinely attentive to their audience, adjusting their message in response to feedback, questions, and non-verbal cues. Empathy is closely related—the ability to understand and consider the perspective, knowledge level, and emotional state of the person you're communicating with allows you to tailor your message appropriately. Confidence matters too—people are more persuaded by communicators who speak with conviction and authority, though this must be balanced with intellectual humility and the willingness to acknowledge uncertainty. Adaptability is also crucial—the ability to adjust your communication style to different audiences and contexts, from formal presentations to casual conversations, is a mark of a sophisticated communicator. Finally, authenticity—communicating in a way that feels genuine rather than performed—builds trust and makes messages more compelling.

questions.sampleBand8: It's a complex issue, but I think it boils down to a combination of factors. Firstly, performance anxiety plays a significant role; the fear of messing up or not being good enough can be paralysing. questions.sampleBand9: I believe the difficulty stems from a confluence of psychological and experiential elements. At its core, public speaking often triggers a deep-seated fear of judgment and potential humiliation. This anxiety can be compounded by a lack of familiarity with public speaking situations; the more unfamiliar the setting, the more pronounced the anxiety tends to be. Additionally, some individuals are more prone to social anxiety, making them particularly susceptible to the pressures of performing in front of an audience. They may feel as though they are walking on eggshells.
questions.sampleAnswer: Public speaking anxiety is extraordinarily common—surveys consistently rank it among the most widespread fears, sometimes above the fear of death. The psychological roots are well understood. At a fundamental level, being observed and evaluated by a group of people triggers the same threat-response mechanisms that evolved to protect us from social rejection, which in ancestral environments could be genuinely dangerous. The fear of negative evaluation—of being judged as incompetent, boring, or foolish—is particularly powerful because it threatens our sense of social standing and self-worth. There's also the performance pressure that comes from knowing that everyone's attention is focused on you simultaneously, which creates a heightened self-consciousness that can interfere with natural, fluent communication. Past negative experiences—a speech that went badly, being laughed at, forgetting what you wanted to say—can create lasting associations that make future public speaking feel threatening. Perfectionism also plays a role: people who hold themselves to very high standards find the possibility of visible failure in front of an audience particularly distressing.

questions.prompt: How important is body language in communication?

questions.sampleBand8: Absolutely, body language is incredibly important. It's often said that communication is only a small percentage verbal, with the rest being non-verbal cues. I think, at the end of the day, it’s essential for building rapport and understanding someone's true intentions. Cultural differences also play a role, of course.
questions.sampleBand9: I'd argue that body language is absolutely paramount in effective communication. While verbal communication conveys the explicit message, non-verbal cues fill in the gaps, providing context and revealing underlying emotions. Moreover, reading between the lines, by observing someone's micro-expressions or posture, can be crucial in understanding their true feelings and intentions. In fact, some research suggests that non-verbal communication accounts for a significant majority of the impact of any interaction. To put it another way, it’s often not what you say, but *how* you say it that truly matters. Being attuned to these subtleties is key to successful interpersonal relationships.
questions.sampleAnswer: Body language is extraordinarily important—research suggests that in face-to-face communication, non-verbal signals including posture, facial expressions, eye contact, gestures, and tone of voice convey a substantial portion of the emotional meaning of a message, often more than the words themselves. When there's a mismatch between what someone says and how their body communicates—when words express confidence but posture signals anxiety, for example—people tend to trust the non-verbal signal over the verbal one. This is because non-verbal communication is largely involuntary and therefore perceived as more authentic. In professional contexts, body language significantly affects how people are perceived—confident posture, appropriate eye contact, and open gestures tend to increase perceptions of competence and trustworthiness. Cultural differences in body language are also important to understand—gestures, personal space norms, and eye contact conventions vary considerably across cultures, and misreading these signals can lead to significant misunderstandings. In the age of video communication, some of these non-verbal cues are partially lost, which is one reason why video calls can feel more tiring than face-to-face conversations.

questions.uzSampleAnswer: Tana tili juda ham muhim—tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatadiki, yuzma-yuz muloqotda noverbal signallar, jumladan, qomat, yuz ifodalari, ko'z bilan aloqa, imo-ishoralar va ovoz ohangi xabarning hissiy ma'nosining katta qismini, ko'pincha so'zlarning o'zidan ham ko'proq yetkazadi. questions.sampleBand9: Without a doubt, social media has fundamentally reshaped the landscape of human communication. It's democratised information sharing and opened up avenues for global connectivity that were previously unimaginable. However, this ease of communication cuts both ways. The ephemeral nature of online interactions can foster superficial relationships, and the lack of non-verbal cues often leads to misinterpretations and conflict. Moreover, the curated reality presented on social media platforms can breed anxiety and social comparison. The jury's still out on the long-term effects, but it's clear that the way we communicate has been irrevocably altered.
questions.sampleAnswer: Profoundly, and in ways that are both positive and concerning. On the positive side, social media has made it easier to maintain connections with a larger number of people across greater distances—it's now possible to stay in touch with acquaintances, former colleagues, and distant family members in ways that would have required significant effort in the pre-social media era. It has also given people new ways to find and connect with others who share their interests, creating communities around niche topics that might not have been viable in a purely local context. However, the concerns are significant. Social media communication tends to be more performative and less authentic than face-to-face interaction—people curate their online presence carefully, presenting an idealised version of themselves rather than communicating honestly. The brevity and informality of social media communication may be eroding people's capacity for sustained, nuanced dialogue. There's also evidence that social media can increase social comparison and feelings of inadequacy, and that the algorithmic amplification of outrage and conflict is making public discourse more polarised and less civil. The net effect on human communication is genuinely complex and still being understood.

The nature of writing might be changing – becoming more informal and direct in some contexts – but its importance, in my opinion, is still paramount. questions.sampleBand9: That's a fascinating question. I would argue that written communication is undergoing a significant transformation, but its fundamental importance remains undiminished. While the immediacy and visual appeal of platforms like TikTok and Instagram are undeniable, the ability to convey complex ideas and nuanced arguments through written language is still indispensable, particularly in fields like law, science, and journalism. We're seeing a shift towards more concise and accessible writing styles, but the core principles of clarity, coherence, and precision are as relevant as ever. In fact, in an age of information overload, the ability to cut through the noise and communicate effectively in writing is arguably *more* important than ever before. questions.sampleAnswer: I think written communication is, paradoxically, becoming both more prevalent and in some ways less valued simultaneously. On one hand, we write more than ever before—the volume of text produced through emails, messages, social media posts, and digital documents is historically unprecedented. In this sense, written communication has never been more central to daily life. On the other hand, the quality and formality of much written communication has declined—the informality of messaging culture, with its abbreviations, emojis, and tolerance for grammatical errors, represents a significant departure from the standards of formal written communication that were expected in previous generations. There's a growing concern that people's ability to write clearly, precisely, and at length is being eroded by the dominance of short-form, informal digital communication. In professional and academic contexts, however, the ability to write well remains highly valued and increasingly differentiating—as AI tools take over more routine writing tasks, the capacity for genuinely sophisticated written communication becomes more rather than less important.

Bu qiymatning pasayishidan ko'ra, rivojlanayotgan landshaftga moslashish haqida ko'proq. Oxir-oqibat, u hali ham muhim.
questions.uzSampleBand9: Bu hayratlanarli savol. Men yozma muloqot sezilarli o'zgarishlarga duch kelayotganini, lekin uning asosiy ahamiyati o'zgarmasligini ta'kidlagan bo'lardim. TikTok va Instagram kabi platformalarning tezkorligi va vizual jozibadorligi inkor etib bo'lmas bo'lsa-da, murakkab g'oyalar va nozik dalillarni yozma tilda ifoda eta olish, ayniqsa huquq, fan va jurnalistika kabi sohalarda hali ham zarur. Biz yozuv uslublarining yanada qisqa va tushunarli bo'lishiga o'tishni ko'rmoqdamiz, ammo aniqlik, izchillik va aniqlikning asosiy tamoyillari har qachongidan ham dolzarbdir. Aslida, axborotning haddan tashqari ko'pligi davrida shovqinni kesib o'tish va yozma ravishda samarali muloqot qilish qobiliyati har qachongidan ham *ko'proq* muhimdir, deyish mumkin. Bu zamon bilan hamnafas bo'lish va yozuvdan to'liq foydalanish haqida va u ayniqsa kasbiy rivojlanish uchun foydali.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Menimcha, yozma muloqot, paradoksal tarzda, ham tobora keng tarqalmoqda, ham bir qator jihatlarda unchalik qadrlanmayapti. Bir tomondan, biz hech qachongidan ham ko'proq yozamiz—elektron pochta, xabarlar, ijtimoiy tarmoqlardagi postlar va raqamli hujjatlar orqali yaratilgan matn hajmi tarixda misli ko'rilmagan. Shu ma'noda, yozma muloqot hech qachon kundalik hayot uchun bunchalik markaziy bo'lmagan. Boshqa tomondan, ko'pgina yozma muloqotlarning sifati va rasmiyligi pasaydi—xabar almashish madaniyatining norasmiyligi, o'zining qisqartmalari, emojilari va grammatik xatolarga toqati bilan, avvalgi avlodlarda kutilgan rasmiy yozma muloqot standartlaridan sezilarli darajada farq qiladi. Odamlarning aniq, to'liq va uzoq yozish qobiliyati qisqa shakldagi, norasmiy raqamli muloqotning hukmronligi tufayli yemirilayotganidan xavotir bor. Biroq, professional va akademik kontekstlarda yaxshi yozish qobiliyati hali ham yuqori qadrlanadi va tobora ajralib turadi—AI vositalari ko'proq oddiy yozuv vazifalarini o'z zimmasiga olar ekan, chinakam murakkab yozma muloqot qobiliyati kam emas, balki ko'proq ahamiyatga ega bo'ladi.

vocabulary.title: Q17 - What Makes a Speech Memorable
sentenceStarters: The most celebrated speeches in history...

questions.sampleBand5: Well, um, I think a speech is memorable if it's, like, really interesting. And, um, if the person speaking is, you know, easy to understand. Yeah, that's it. It, um, sticks in your head.
questions.sampleBand6: I mean, what makes a speech memorable? I think it's a combination of things. Basically, the content has to be engaging, right? And also, the speaker needs to be a good communicator. If they can, you know, get their point across clearly, people will remember it better, I think. And maybe a touch of humour.
questions.sampleBand7: Well, a memorable speech, certainly, has to have strong content. It needs to be something that grabs your attention and gives you something to think about afterwards. Moreover, the delivery is crucial. A good speaker can captivate an audience, even if the topic isn't inherently fascinating. It's about connecting with people and making an impact. And a bit of story telling helps.
questions.sampleBand8: I think several elements contribute to a speech being memorable. Obviously, the content is important; it should be insightful, original, or thought-provoking. But equally important is the speaker's ability to connect with the audience. They need to be passionate about what they're saying and bring it to life. Furthermore, a speech that evokes emotion, whether it's laughter, sadness, or inspiration, is more likely to leave a lasting impression. And perhaps a memorable quote.
questions.sampleBand9: What makes a speech truly memorable? It's a multifaceted thing. Undoubtedly, the content needs to be compelling – offering fresh perspectives, challenging assumptions, or presenting complex ideas in an accessible way. Actions speak louder than words, so compelling storytelling is essential. But beyond that, it's about the speaker's ability to forge a connection with the audience, to draw them in with their charisma and authenticity. A speech that resonates emotionally, perhaps by tapping into shared values or aspirations, will stand the test of time. The cherry on the cake is a powerful delivery that is both engaging and confident.
questions.sampleAnswer: The most memorable speeches share several qualities that distinguish them from competent but forgettable communication. First, a clear and compelling central idea—the best speeches are organised around a single powerful insight or argument that the audience can carry away with them. Second, emotional resonance—speeches that connect with the audience's feelings, values, and experiences are far more memorable than purely informational presentations. The most celebrated speeches in history—from Martin Luther King's 'I Have a Dream' to Churchill's wartime addresses—work because they speak to something deep in human experience. Third, vivid, concrete language—abstract arguments become memorable when they're illustrated with specific stories, images, and examples that make ideas tangible. Fourth, authenticity—audiences can sense when a speaker genuinely believes what they're saying, and this conviction is itself compelling. Fifth, structure—a speech with a clear beginning, middle, and end, with a satisfying arc, is easier to follow and remember than one that meanders. Finally, delivery matters enormously—pace, pause, tone, and physical presence all contribute to whether a speech lands or falls flat. The combination of all these elements, when they work together, creates the kind of speech that people remember years later.
questions.uzSampleBand5: Xo'sh, e-e, menimcha, nutq agar juda qiziqarli bo'lsa, esda qolarli bo'ladi. Va, e-e, agar gapirayotgan odam, bilasizmi, tushunarli bo'lsa. Ha, shu. U, e-e, esingizda qoladi.
questions.uzSampleBand6: Aytmoqchimanki, nutqni nima esda qolarli qiladi? Menimcha, bu narsalarning kombinatsiyasi. Asosan, mazmun qiziqarli bo'lishi kerak, to'g'rimi? Va, shuningdek, notiq yaxshi muloqotchi bo'lishi kerak. Agar ular, bilasizmi, o'z fikrlarini aniq yetkaza olsalar, odamlar buni yaxshiroq eslashadi, menimcha. Va balki bir oz hazil.
questions.uzSampleBand7: Xo'sh, esda qolarli nutq, albatta, kuchli mazmunga ega bo'lishi kerak. U e'tiboringizni tortadigan va keyin o'ylab ko'rishga arziydigan narsa bo'lishi kerak. Bundan tashqari, yetkazib berish juda muhim. Yaxshi notiq, hatto mavzu unchalik qiziqarli bo'lmasa ham, tomoshabinlarni o'ziga jalb qila oladi. Gap odamlar bilan bog'lanish va ta'sir o'tkazish haqida. Va bir oz hikoya aytish yordam beradi.
questions.uzSampleBand8: Menimcha, bir nechta elementlar nutqning esda qolarli bo'lishiga hissa qo'shadi. Albatta, mazmun muhim; u chuqur, original yoki fikr yuritishga undaydigan bo'lishi kerak. Ammo notiqning tomoshabinlar bilan bog'lana olish qobiliyati ham muhim. Ular aytayotgan narsaga qiziqishi kerak va uni jonlantirishi kerak. Bundan tashqari, kulgi, qayg'u yoki ilhom bo'ladimi, hissiyot uyg'otadigan nutq unutilmas taassurot qoldirishi ehtimoli ko'proq. Va ehtimol esda qolarli iqtibos.
questions.uzSampleBand9: Nutqni chindan ham esda qolarli qiladigan narsa nima? Bu ko'p qirrali narsa. Shubhasiz, mazmun ishonchli bo'lishi kerak - yangi nuqtai nazarlarni taklif qilish, taxminlarni shubha ostiga qo'yish yoki murakkab g'oyalarni tushunarli tarzda taqdim etish. Amallar so'zlardan ko'ra balandroq gapiradi, shuning uchun qiziqarli hikoya aytish muhim. Ammo bundan tashqari, gap notiqning tomoshabinlar bilan aloqa o'rnatish, ularni o'zining jozibasi va haqiqiyligi bilan o'ziga jalb qilish qobiliyatida. Hissiy jihatdan rezonanslashadigan nutq, ehtimol umumiy qadriyatlar yoki intilishlarga tegish orqali, vaqt sinovidan o'tadi. Tortning ustidagi gilos - bu ham qiziqarli, ham ishonchli bo'lgan kuchli yetkazib berish.
questions.uzSampleAnswer: Eng esda qolarli nutqlar ularni malakali, ammo unutiladigan muloqotdan ajratib turadigan bir nechta sifatlarga ega. Birinchidan, aniq va ishonchli asosiy g'oya - eng yaxshi nutqlar tomoshabinlar o'zlari bilan olib ketishi mumkin bo'lgan bitta kuchli tushuncha yoki argument atrofida tashkil etiladi. Ikkinchidan, hissiy rezonans - tomoshabinlarning his-tuyg'ulari, qadriyatlari va tajribalari bilan bog'liq bo'lgan nutqlar shunchaki axborot taqdimotlariga qaraganda ancha esda qolarli. Tarixdagi eng mashhur nutqlar - Martin Lyuter Kingning "Mening orzularim bor" nutqidan tortib Cherchillning urush davridagi murojaatlarigacha - ular inson tajribasida chuqur narsaga murojaat qilganligi sababli ishlaydi. Uchinchidan, yorqin, aniq til - mavhum argumentlar g'oyalarni aniq qiladigan o'ziga xos hikoyalar, tasvirlar va misollar bilan tasvirlanganda esda qolarli bo'ladi. To'rtinchidan, haqiqiylik - tomoshabinlar notiqning aytayotganiga chin dildan ishonishini sezishlari mumkin va bu ishonchning o'zi ham ishonchli. Beshinchidan, tuzilma - aniq boshlanishi, o'rtasi va oxiri bo'lgan, qoniqarli yoyga ega bo'lgan nutq chalkash nutqqa qaraganda osonroq tushuniladi va esda qoladi. Nihoyat, yetkazib berish juda muhim - tezlik, pauza, ohang va jismoniy mavjudlik nutqning muvaffaqiyatli yoki muvaffaqiyatsiz bo'lishiga ta'sir qiladi. Barcha ushbu elementlarning kombinatsiyasi birgalikda ishlaganda, odamlar yillar o'tib eslaydigan nutqni yaratadi.
